chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Rooming with the bass and baritone players
summary: Smith roomed with the bassist or baritone player and knew Sidney deParis, while his wife stayed in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you room with anybody in particular?
Yeah. I had the bass player. (?) John. The bass player, he and I would sleep together; we would room together.
Wasn't the bass player Bob Iziguirra(?)? I.e. Izaguirre

No. Let me see, what is the bass player's name? I forget now. No, the one I'm thinking about, the ...(?)., his name is John, a big yellow... He looked like Lester Young. Big-eyed yellow boy. Yeah, he was with Snub. Sidney deParis was his trumpet. He was with Don. He had a bunch of fellows who I didn't know. And some of the boys was from Panama. The baritone player, he and I roomed mostly together all the time.
I can't think of his name. Well, ...(?). played first alto. A little-bitty old brown-skinned fellow. He was nice. Sometimes I roomed with him. I mostly stayed by myself.
You didn't have your wife along.
No, no. I didn't my wife then. My wife was in Kansas City.
